subject: music
title: Texture and Orchestration
welcome_lead: Monophonic, homophonic, polyphonic — and how composers layer the orchestra.
meta_desc: A-Level Music: texture types and orchestration analysis.
final_note: Texture is the listener's first impression.

concepts.def: Simultaneous variations of the same melody.
Solo or small-group passage in opposition to tutti.

walkthroughs.body_html: Monophonic — Gregorian chant. Homophonic — Classical melody-and-accompaniment. Polyphonic — Bach fugue with independent voices. Most pieces shift between textures.

Note the number of independent parts, their relationship (imitation, parallel, contrary), and the use of tutti vs reduced forces. Orchestration choices — pizzicato strings, muted brass — shape texture.
In a concerto, tutti (ripieno) and concertante (solo) sections alternate. Texture becomes structural — Vivaldi's Four Seasons shows clear ripieno/solo contrast.
